title: Oracle Sees Massive Trading Surge After Selloff
detail:
Oracle Sees Massive Trading Surge After Selloff
Moz Farooque ACCA
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 12:48 PM MST 2 min read
ORCL
Trade Oracle on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) saw trading activity surge to its highest level in at least a year as investors piled back into the stock following a sharp post-fundraising selloff.

Roughly 84.3 million Oracle shares changed hands on Tuesday, November 3, up 44% from about 58.4 million a day earlier. The stock gained 5.85% to $126.19, snapping back after falling roughly 9% Monday.

ORCL GF Value chart

The rebound came after an ugly stretch.

Oracle had fallen 18.58% across the prior three trading sessions, pressured by concern over the company's $20 billion financing plan and the enormous capital requirements of its AI and cloud expansion.

The fundraise includes $10 billion in equity and $10 billion in debt. Oracle priced 86.2 million shares at $116, an 11.2% discount to its prior close, while its new fixed-rate bonds carry interest rates ranging from 7% to 8.65%.

That would normally look like a tough setup for existing shareholders.

But investors may be reacting to greater clarity around how much additional capital Oracle actually needs.

Stephens analyst Brett Huff upgraded Oracle to Buy from Hold and raised his price target to $213 from $185, arguing that Oracle's Investor Day reduced one of the biggest uncertainties surrounding the stock.

Oracle now says it requires only about $20 billion of additional external capital to fund its expansion through fiscal 2030, partly because vendors are financing equipment, customers are making upfront capacity payments, and some clients are bringing their own hardware.

Management also expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and reach roughly $30 billion in fiscal 2029.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most interesting part of this move is not simply the 44% volume increase.

It is what investors were buying after.

Oracle had just announced a heavily discounted equity offering, expensive new debt, and another enormous commitment to AI infrastructure. Yet instead of continuing to sell the stock, traders came back aggressively once the financing path became clearer.

That suggests the market may have been more worried about uncapped funding needs than the dilution itself.

Still, one rebound does not settle the debate.

Oracle already had about $125.3 billion in borrowings as of August 31, and the company still needs its AI investments to generate enough growth and cash flow to justify those obligations.

Tech stocks were mixed late Wednesday afternoon, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) rising 0.3% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF (XSD) falling 3.2%.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor index declined 3.6%.

In sector news, Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections could lead to stricter data-center restrictions, negatively affecting artificial intelligence sentiment, Morgan Stanley said in a note. The firm said the practical risk they see is that new state-level policies could create a divide between US regions that allow new data centers and those that restrict them.

In corporate news, Datadog (DDOG) shares fell past 14% after the cloud monitoring and security platform issued a soft Q4 revenue forecast, signaling a growth deceleration despite Q3 results topping consensus estimates.

Oracle (ORCL) has axed a $7 billion chip-leasing contract with Tencent, yielding to pressure from the White House, the Financial Times reported. Oracle shares were down 1.4%.

Apple (AAPL) has reduced employee spending allowances for AI tools as part of a broader cost-cutting effort, Bloomberg reported. Apple shares were up 6.2%.

Arista Networks (ANET) shares rose 4.7% after the networking equipment maker raised the midpoint of its full-year revenue outlook amid accelerating product demand and supply chain efficiency.

title: Accenture vs. Oracle: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2027?
detail:
Accenture vs. Oracle: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2027?
Mike Schwenk, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 10:20 AM MST 8 min read
ACN
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors weighing Accenture (NYSE:ACN) against Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) in 2026 are looking at two very different ways to play the ongoing digital transformation of the global enterprise.

Choosing between them requires understanding whether you prefer a services-led or an infrastructure-led approach to tech growth.

Accenture provides high-level consulting and implementation services for large organizations, while Oracle supplies the underlying database and cloud infrastructure that powers those same companies.

Both are critical players in the software and cloud landscape, but they offer different market exposure through specialized services versus mission-critical hardware and cloud hosting applications.

The case for Accenture

Accenture sells professional services, such as strategy and consulting, to large businesses across the information technology landscape. It maintains deep relationships with more than 9,000 clients, including roughly three-quarters of the Fortune Global 500 and every G7 government.

The company counts 317 "Diamond" clients, its largest accounts, and its 18 key ecosystem partners, together representing about 65% of fiscal 2026 revenue.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Aug. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $74.2 billion, representing approximately 6.5% growth from the previous year.

The company reported net income attributable to shareholders of about $8.4 billion for the same period. This resulted in a net margin of close to 11.3%, which tracks slightly higher than the 11% seen during fiscal year 2025.

New bookings for the year came to $84.5 billion, ahead of revenue, and fourth-quarter bookings of $22.2 billion ran at 1.2 times revenue. For fiscal 2027, management guides to revenue growth of 3% to 6% in local currency, with acquisitions expected to contribute 2 to 2.5 percentage points to that growth, diluted earnings per share of $14.39 to $14.81, and free cash flow of $11.0 billion to $11.8 billion.

At its Oct. 14, 2026 investor day, management laid out an ambition of mid-single-digit revenue growth in local currency for fiscal 2027 and 2028, and it plans to return at least $9.5 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2027.

As of its Aug. 31, 2026 balance sheet, total borrowings of about $10.1 billion against total shareholders' equity of $32.7 billion give a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.3x, measured on balance-sheet debt and excluding lease liabilities.

Long-term debt doubled during the year as the company funded about $4.9 billion in acquisitions, and it has kept buying since then, closing four small deals in October alone. The current ratio, which measures assets available to cover short-term liabilities, sits at approximately 1.4x.

Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) is lining up $20 billion in fresh funding, but investors face a bigger bill. Shares fell 2.16% to $121.50 at 9.13 a.m. ET in November 4 premarket trading. The cloud infrastructure provider expects its debt and equity offerings to close November 4, subject to customary conditions. That remains an expected closing, rather than confirmation that the money has arrived.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with ORCL.

Is ORCL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

ORCL GF Value chart

The package adds 86,206,897 shares at an offering price of $116 apiece and $10 billion in bonds across five tranches carrying coupons of 7% to 8.65%. Estimated combined net proceeds reach approximately $19.9 billion. Reuters reported that the fundraising supports Oracle's AI expansion, while the company's stated uses also cover refinancing and other corporate needs. More funding could help turn cloud demand into operating capacity, although existing shareholders absorb dilution along the way.

The debt brings approximately $776.75 million in annual coupon paymentsa principal-weighted rate of 7.77%, excluding issuance costs. That raises the hurdle for infrastructure returns. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 89/100, with profitability and growth standing out while financial strength, valuation and momentum lag those strengths. The business has operating muscle, but the financing makes cash generation increasingly important: new capacity needs to produce enough cash to cover borrowing costs and justify the larger share count.

Investing.com -- Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) reported FQ3 2026 on Nov 3. Revenue was $13.38B against a $13.06B estimate, and EPS was $2.09 against $1.94 (+7.7%). Even so, the stock traded at $487.08 (+0.66%) as of Nov 4, 12:25 PM EST. The after-hours print of $518.99 (+7.25%) has faded. The stock is down 15.8% over the past week and 23.2% over the past month, and it sits well below its 52-week high of $658.52. The market had already priced in a strong quarter.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Questions Answered

Is AI GPU revenue real? Mostly yes. Data Center revenue rose 97% to a record $8.5B and is now 64% of sales. MI455x volume shipments began in Q3. Early Helios racks are online at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle. Read more (Nov 4, 2026)

Is the guidance strong enough? Q4 revenue is guided to about $17.0B, up 66% year over year. Consensus was around $16.2B. Management also guided 2027 revenue growth above 80%. Stifel notes that Data Center AI should pass server CPUs for the first time in Q4. Read more (Nov 4, 2026)

Are margins holding? Yes. Adjusted gross margin was 56% and adjusted operating margin 29%. Gross margin has stayed at 54–57% for the last five quarters, apart from a 43.2% dip in June 2025. Read more

Is server CPU demand just a side story? No. Server revenue more than doubled. KeyBanc now expects server CPU revenue to double in 2027, against a prior 70% growth estimate. Jefferies models over $40B. Read more

Questions Still Open

Client weakness: Client & Gaming fell 8% to $3.7B. KeyBanc expects Client to drop more than 20% sequentially in Q4, and PCs to decline in 2027.

Dilution from customer deals: The OpenAI and Meta warrants triggered a roughly $1B quarterly charge. CFO Jean Hu said the warrants begin diluting shareholders once shipment and commercial vesting conditions are met. More guidance on timing is promised in 2027. The deal with Anthropic includes an AMD investment in that company. Read more (Nov 3, 2026)

Valuation: The forward P/E is 60.5x (FQ ending Dec 31, 2026). InvestingPro fair value is $441.42, which puts the stock about 9.3% above fair value. The analyst target upside is +33.1%. All values as of Nov 4, 2026.

Next Catalysts

Q4 delivery. The $17.0B guide needs GPU revenue to jump sharply. Susquehanna models about $6.8B of GPU revenue. The next release is tentatively set for Feb 2, 2027, with consensus at EPS $2.68 and revenue $16.31B. Consensus has not yet caught up to the guide.

Estimate resets. Susquehanna raised its 2027 revenue estimate to about $95.5B. Consensus is $90.83B (FY2027) and $126.79B (FY2028). Revisions have been small so far: +0.27% for EPS over 30 days.

Helios ramp. Watch for additional rack deployments and new customers.

Warrant timing. Any 2027 update on vesting would set the size of the dilution.

Price targets. Recent targets are Stifel $725, KeyBanc $725, Susquehanna $650, Jefferies $650 and Truist $605.
